body_paragraphs: A new mobile product with no legacy roadmap, built around one of the largest audiences online, is the kind of work I want to do next. I am a consumer product manager in Seattle, and owning a feature area from first spec to the metric that tells you whether it worked is exactly how I like to operate.

At Brightpath I own growth for an app with 12M monthly users and run more than 60 A/B tests a year, so I set success metrics before anything ships. I rebuilt onboarding and moved day-7 retention from 31% to 39%. At Tidewell I redesigned bank linking for consumer financial data and cut drop-off by 28%, working daily with design and engineering.

I have not built a product from zero, and I would be learning your audience quickly. I would bring tight specs, a test-first habit and a willingness to work in the details of the build alongside engineers. I would welcome a conversation about which feature area you have in mind and how the team works day to day.

autofill.why do you want to work at mrbeast?: I want to build a consumer mobile product from the ground up, and an interactive community around an audience this size is a rare chance to do it. autofill.describe how you use data to decide what: I define the metric before I build. At Brightpath I run 60+ A/B tests a year with a 38% win rate, and I read results by cohort rather than headline lift. When I rebuilt onboarding, the cohort view showed the personalised first session was driving day-7 retention from 31% to 39%, so we invested further there.
autofill.tell us about a product you shipped on m: At Tidewell I shipped automated round-up savings for a budgeting app with 3M users. I interviewed users, wrote the requirements with design and engineering, and launched it in stages. Monthly active savers grew 47% in two quarters, and we used the same metrics to decide what to iterate on next.
autofill._default: I enjoy owning a consumer product end to end, from user research and specs to launch metrics. This role matches my mobile growth work at Brightpath, and the zero-to-one scope is what draws me most. I would be glad to talk through how I would approach a feature area.

cover_letter.name: Kikoff cover letter
body_paragraphs: Kikoff helps people build financial security with affordable tools, and the product team is asked to find what keeps those users coming back. Engagement built on real data and real conversations is the part of product work I enjoy most, so the Product Manager role in San Francisco reads like a description of my best projects.

At Tidewell, a consumer fintech app with 3M users, I introduced push and email lifecycle messaging that reactivated 180K dormant users, and I cut sign-up drop-off by 28% with a clearer bank-linking flow. At Brightpath I run 60+ experiments a year and pull the cuts myself in SQL, which is how I found that a personalised first session lifted day-7 retention from 31% to 39%.

Hands-on copywriting and content have been a smaller part of my work, and I would build that skill with your team. I like to learn from users first, so I would welcome a conversation about the engagement loops you are trying to build and the data you already have on them. I can share examples of readouts I have written.

autofill.why do you want to work at kikoff?: I want to work on consumer finance products that help people become more secure, and engagement is the part I know best. At Tidewell, lifecycle messaging reactivated 180K dormant users of a budgeting app, and I saw how much it mattered to them. Kikoff's focus on affordable tools and data-driven product work is a strong match.
autofill.describe how you find insights in data t: I start by cutting the data into segments, then look for the behavior that separates retained users from lapsed ones. At Brightpath I pulled this in SQL and found that users who finished a personalised first session came back far more often. We rebuilt onboarding around it, and day-7 retention went from 31% to 39%.
autofill.tell us about a time you talked to users: At Marlow Market I ran weekly user interviews with shoppers and sellers, and the same checkout complaints came up repeatedly. I wrote them into 40+ PRDs and the findings shaped the mobile checkout rebuild. I still start most projects with five to ten conversations before I look at a single dashboard.
autofill._default: I am drawn to this role because it centers on understanding users through data and conversations and then building engagement around what I learn. It matches my lifecycle and growth work at Tidewell and Brightpath, and I would enjoy applying it to consumer finance.
